top_categories.workout_context: 132ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Gran Fondo Pirineus, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
11,811ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
11,811ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Pirineus. Train it until it feels boring.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Pirineus' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Pirineus. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 89 miles.
At mile 60 of 89, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 89 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 11,811ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 89 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 11,811ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.weather: June in Camprodon, Girona, Spain. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Pirineus. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Pirineus’s 89 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Gran Fondo Pirineus includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Pirineus rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and VO2max to prepare you for 89 miles of mixed terrain in Camprodon, Girona, Spain.
